QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_46

question.text: In the duration-based hedge ratio formula, what does 'futures duration' refer to?

answer.text: The modified duration of the bond underlying the futures contract
The time remaining until the futures contract expires
The average duration of all bonds in the portfolio
The duration of the risk-free rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures duration is the modified duration of the bond underlying the futures contract — the "Futures Modified Duration" used in the denominator of the hedge ratio formula. For example, bond futures may have a modified duration of 4.7 years, and this value drives how the futures price responds to yield changes. The Trap: Time to expiry is not the same as duration. Portfolio duration is in the numerator, not denominator. The risk-free rate doesn't have a meaningful duration concept here. Note: Always match the duration measure to the contract: use the modified duration of the bond underlying the futures contract in the denominator and the portfolio's modified duration in the numerator.
